betterCitation: Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart, chapter 19, the feast in Mbanta (one of the oldest members of the umunna) (William Heinemann, 1958)
reason: The wording holds. The chapter 19 text at esl-bits.eu gives the three sentences exactly, and gives their order, which was the thing worth testing since the middle sentence could plausibly have stood first: it runs When we gather together in the moonlit village ground it is not because of the moon. Every man can see it in his own compound. We come together because it is good for kinsmen to do so. That is the quotation as proposed. The chapter is right and the scene is right: Okonkwo's last year of exile in his motherland, the feast for his mother's kinsmen before he returns to Umuofia, and Mbanta is named in the chapter. Written in English, so there is no translation to drift. Dropping the unverified Penguin 2001 page was the correct call and the first edition, William Heinemann 1958, is the right thing to name in its place. shipped.js: nothing shipped, nothing near, Achebe at zero for the year, not banned, once in September. Tag Fiction, pre-2000, publishable, no misattribution trap, source line leads with the name, no dash, 125 characters. Not refuted. One improvement offered rather than a fault: the source says an elder of the umunna where the novel says one of the oldest members of the umunna rose to thank Okonkwo, and the verifier's own speaker field keeps that phrase while the printed line loses it. The text's phrase is not a paraphrase and it fits, at 133 characters, if farewell is dropped from the feast; the feast is plainly a leave-taking in context and the word is not carrying the locator. betterCitation gives that form.
